# The provenance file on Átropos

*The provenance file for Átropos. Nothing here is unsourced; that is what the file is for.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **Ἄτροπος** — "Inflexible, inevitable". On record: Hesiod, Theogony 217, 904–906 (the two genealogies of the Moirai), Homer, Iliad 22.179–185 (Zeus and the decree of Moira), Bacchylides 5.94–154 and Hesiod, Catalogue of Women fr. 280 (Méleagros and the brand); Ovid, Metamorphoses 8.451ff, Plato, Republic 617c–d (the spindle of Necessity).

**2. The preserved evidence.** **a → Á** (Acute on a) — absent from the ASCII form *atropos*, present in the restoration, verifiable against the sources above.

**3. The narrative record.** **Daughters of Night** — Hesiod gives her two genealogies, and the doublet is the message.  In the Theogony’s first account (217) the Moirai — Klōthṓ, Láchesis, and Átropos, “who give mortals good and evil when they are born” — are fatherless daughters of Nyx, Night, sisters of Death and Sleep: older than Zeus, bound to no one’s throne. **Méleagros and the Brand** — Seven days after Méleagros was born, the three sisters came to his mother Althaia in her chamber.  Klōthṓ and Láchesis promised the child strength and daring; Átropos, pointing to the brand blazing on the hearth, pronounced that he would live only until it was wholly burned.

**4. The physical record.** The Moirai rarely received independent cult — Pausanias (8.37.1) records an altar of the Fates beside the sanctuary of Despoina at Lycosura, and the cult title Zeus Moiragetēs, “leader of the Fates,” is attested in Arcadian worship. Their true monument is funerary: Roman sarcophagi carved the Parcae with spindle, scroll, and shears as standard eschatological furniture, and Hellenistic gems show Átropos with her blades. The spindle-whorl dedications of spinning-women’s tools found in temple deposits tie the goddess’s craft to real women’s work.

**5. The current holding.** The temple at [/atropos/](/atropos/), classified Tier 2. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

**6. The documented resonances.** **Insurance & Protection Services**, **Timekeeping & Calendar Systems**, **Legal, Justice & Compliance** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/atropos/blog/resonance/).

**7. The primary sources.** [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**8. The continuing record.** Shakespeare's "thread of life" and every three-weird-sisters scene from Macbeth to modern fantasy descend from her triad.  In philosophy she anchors the ancient debate on determinism: Chrysippus and the Stoics built their heimarmenē around the Moirai's decree, and Epicurus invented the atomic swerve partly to break Átropos' loom.
